ov: A huge, semi-aquatic grazer that spends its days in African rivers and lakes and comes out at night to feed. Its closest living relatives are whales and dolphins.

why.dg: Aggressive and unpredictable, and counted among the most dangerous animals in the world.
why.ac: Stays in water or mud to keep cool by day, then comes out at dusk to graze.

rg: Rivers, lakes and swamps of sub-Saharan Africa, with grassland nearby to graze.
df: Almost entirely grass: about 40 kg a night, gathered on walks of 3–5 km from the water.
